request.description: launch: run a Lua script in the bundled lua-dap-server (program), or start a program that loads lua-debug-module, e.g. a LÖVE game (runtimeExecutable). attach: connect to a program that is already running and loaded lua-debug-module (require("luadebug").start()); set port (and host).

program.description: launch: absolute path to the Lua file to debug

preset.description: Defaults for a known host, for anything this entry doesn't set. love (LÖVE 11+): luaVersion luajit, sourceRoot ${workspaceFolder}, errorHandler [love.errorhandler, love.errhand], onTerminate love.event.quit; for launch, runtimeExecutable lovec (Windows) or love, with runtimeArgs [sourceRoot].

sourceRoot.description: attach / runtimeExecutable: the folder the program loads its scripts from; relative chunk names (@main.lua) resolve against it, so breakpoints match

errorHandler.description: attach / runtimeExecutable: global function(s) the program calls as its xpcall message handler, e.g. ["love.errorhandler", "love.errhand"]. Each is wrapped, also if it's defined later, so uncaught errors stop in the debugger.

onTerminate.description: attach / runtimeExecutable: global function called to end the program when the debugger stops it, e.g. love.event.quit. Without one, the debugger raises an error in the program.

runtimeExecutable.description: launch: a program to start and debug instead of running program, e.g. "lovec.exe" for a LÖVE game. A bare name is looked up on PATH (including the user and system PATH). The program must load the debugger: if os.getenv("LUADEBUG_PORT") then require("luadebug").start() end

runtimeArgs.description: launch: arguments for runtimeExecutable, e.g. ["${workspaceFolder}"] for the game folder

env.description: launch with runtimeExecutable: extra environment variables for the program; null removes one

modulePath.description: launch with runtimeExecutable: luadebug.dll/.so, or the folder holding it; it's put on the program's LUA_CPATH. Defaults to the dap.lua.binary folder, else the folder lua-dap-server is in.

host.description: attach: IPv4 address the program's luadebug.start() listens on

port.description: attach: port the program's luadebug.start() listens on (start()'s default is 8172)

cwd.description: Working directory for the script (or for runtimeExecutable). Relative require()/io paths resolve against it. Defaults to the workspace folder.

args.description: Script arguments: available as the global `arg` table (arg[1..]; arg[0] is the script path), and as `...` on Lua 5.2+.

packagePath.description: Entries prepended to Lua's package.path for this launch, e.g. ["${workspaceFolder}/src/?.lua"]. Searched before any global packagePath (settings.json: lsp.lua-debugger.settings.packagePath) and before Lua's defaults.

packageCpath.description: Entries prepended to Lua's package.cpath for this launch (for .dll/.so modules loaded with require). Same precedence rules as packagePath.

luaVersion.description: Which Lua version's lua-dap-server build to launch. Downloaded automatically from GitHub Releases on first use, per platform.

preloadPaths.description: Folders whose .lua files and .dll/.so C modules are automatically loaded into the global table before the debug target runs. .dll/.so files must export a luaopen_<filename> entry point (the standard Lua C-module convention).

debugServerPath.description: Advanced/testing: exact path to a lua-dap-server binary to launch directly, bypassing luaVersion resolution and the download/cache mechanism entirely. Mainly for testing a locally-built binary before it's part of a release.
